transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Jensen Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Tomás Rivera (Redwood CSM), Lori Martinez (Crescent Procurement), Aaron Blake (Crescent Legal), Priya Nair (Crescent Security), Samir Patel (Crescent ML)

Summary:
Quick procurement/legal sync to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations for Dedicated vs Hosted, pricing approval path and pilot onboarding steps. Security team asked clarifying q's on KMS and data residency. Legal asked about indemnity and subprocessors; AE committed to send redlined MSA and security pack.

Topics: MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets, pilot pricing/discount, dedicated vs hosted, security docs (SOC2/ISO/KMS), sign-off timeline, next steps.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jensen (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, i think we have about 50 ish minutes, want to run through the redlines and make sure procurement and legal are aligned before we send formal quote.
[00:12] Lori (Procurement): yep thanks, we're mostly here to understand risk posture, timeline for procurement approval and what changes in the MSA we should expect.
[00:20] Maya (Redwood SE): quick intro, i'm maya on the SE side, i'll handle the technical answers - particularly around dedicated capacity, private deployment options and how we handle encryption/kms and audit logs.
[00:30] Aaron (Legal): hi all, hi maya. high level - our counsel flagged three big areas: indemnity & liability caps, data processing/security obligations in the DPA, and subprocessors. also curious about SLAs and credits.
[00:45] Jensen: understood, we'll call those out. our standard MSA has a liability cap tied to fees, but we can discuss tiered caps for enterprise; the DPA outlines data handling plus optional addendum for on-prem or VPC installs.
[00:57] Priya (Security): quick Q - how does Redwood manage customer keys? we need to know if we can bring our own keys (BYOK) and whether logs show KMS usage. also data residency - can you guarantee no egress from us-east-2?
[01:12] Maya: yes BYOK is supported for Private deployments and for Dedicated via KMS integrations; in Hosted we recommend customer-managed KMS via our key-wrap approach. about region locking - we can pin workloads to a region, there are operational caveats for failover but it's possible to guarantee primary region residency, will document specifics in the security pack.
[01:30] Samir (ML): and for the pilot we want to run inference latency benchmarks with our seq lengths and kv cache pattern; will you provide a baseline config?
[01:38] Tomás (CSM): yes we typically run a bench with a 7-10 day sample; maya will own config and we'll provide a spreadsheet for results.
[01:45] Aaron: subprocessors - can you provide the list and confirm notification process for changes? procurement will need a subprocessor appendix.
[01:53] Jensen: we have a standard subprocessor list, we'll attach it. we can agree to notify changes and provide a 30 day notice for new subprocessors for enterprise contracts.
[02:03] Lori: about SLA - our vendor policy requires 99.9% uptime for production endpoints and credits for breaches. what SLAs can Redwood commit to for hosted vs dedicated?
[02:14] Maya: hosted API is usually documented at 99.5 for general tiers, but for Dedicated (reserved capacity) we can support SLA 99.9 with a signed enterprise addendum. latency SLOs are provided per model and route - we give p50/p95 numbers and token-throughput guarantees for dedicated pools.
[02:34] Aaron: okay, we need to see the specific SLA language for credits and remedy steps.
[02:39] Jensen: will include SLA addendum draft. for credits we propose service credits scaling with downtime hours - we'll send template.
[02:48] Priya: encryption at rest and in transit fine, but what about KV cache lifetime and log retention? we need audit logs for 12 months, and ability to export them.
[02:58] Maya: audit log retention can be extended as an add-on. KV cache is ephemeral per model instance but you can configure persistent caching for private deployments; logs are exportable to your S3 or SIEM. we'll share specifics.
[03:11] Samir: pricing - procurement asked whether the pilot can use a discounted reserved capacity or a metered hosted plan; threshold for committing to dedicated later?
[03:21] Jensen: two paths: metered hosted with standard per-token/embedding pricing, or a 90-day pilot on a reserved/dedicated pool at a pilot discount; if you convert to full dedicated within 90 days we can roll pilot fees into commitment. we'll put both options in the quote.
[03:36] Lori: procurement needs price deck with ARPA, estimated monthly spend and headroom for burst capacity. also approvals go through our finance committee; range estimates help.
[03:44] Jensen: we'll provide a pricing summary spreadsheet with committed tiers, burst pricing and an example cost model using your monthly token estimates.
[03:51] Aaron: a few legal-specific redline points: can we get a mutual indemnity carveout for willful misconduct, and can liability cap be negotiated to X months of fees?
[03:58] Jensen: yes those are negotiable - we'll propose tiered caps. also note we carry cyber insurance; we can provide cert evidence.
[04:08] Priya: any compliance certifications? SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 required by our policy.
[04:14] Maya: we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001; pen test summary available. i'll include certs and a short architecture diagram showing KMS/HSM flow.
[04:24] Aaron: subprocessors again - please include cloud infra providers and any managed service partners. we need the ability to object to new subprocessors.
[04:31] Jensen: standard process is notice and discussion; for enterprise we can include a right to object for critical subprocessors with remediation options.
[04:40] Lori: timeline - procurement review then legal negotiation, target sign by 2027-02-05 to allow pilot start mid-February. is that achievable?
[04:47] Tomás: yes, we can aim for pilot onboarding by 2027-02-14 if redlines are resolved in the next week.
[04:53] Samir: tech onboarding: we need IP allowlist, test keys and a contact for infra.
[04:58] Maya: i'll be the se contact, i'll share a runbook and a test harness.
[05:05] Aaron: one more on data residency: if you failover outside region due to incident will you notify us and what are the remediation steps?
[05:13] Maya: we have incident procedures; we'll notify within our incident SLA and coordinate data scope - we can add explicit commitments in the DPA for notification windows.
[05:22] Jensen: wrapping up - agreed actions: we'll send redlined MSA/DPA and SLA addendum, security pack, pricing spreadsheet, and propose a legal-only call.
[05:31] Lori: sounds good; procurement will review redline and come back with priorities.
[05:35] Aaron: i can be available for 2027-01-25 afternoon for a legal deep-dive.
[05:40] Jensen: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up by email with the docs and calendar invite for the legal call.

End of transcript.
